title: Autoscaler fingerprint mismatch causing oscillatory scale decisions — mitigation roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a regional capacity event on 2025-02-14 we observed repeated oscillatory scale-ups and scale-downs across Redwood Dedicated pools. Symptoms looked like false-positive scale triggers followed by immediate scale-downs that caused cold-start spikes and elevated tail latency for active customers. Root cause analysis points to a fingerprint mismatch between the KEDA trigger aggregation and the HPA percentile windowing: short-lived probe bursts were amplified by a low-sample aggregation heuristic, producing transient high-percentile signals that were considered eligible for immediate scale decisions. This ticket tracks the mitigation roadmap, required code changes, runbook updates, and observability additions to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-14 03:12 UTC - On-call alerted by SLO burn (increase in 99th of inference latency) for us-east-1-dedicated pool
2025-02-14 03:17 UTC - Ops increased target replicas manually to reduce tail latency; customer reports decreased errors
2025-02-14 03:40 UTC - Scale-downs started as autoscaler observed metric drop; subsequent cold-starts reintroduced latency spikes
2025-02-14 04:05 UTC - Engineering engaged for correlation of KEDA trigger counts, HPA metrics, and probe logs

2025-02-14 05:10 UTC - Preliminary RCA: short bursts from health probes and ephemeral request bursts produced high-percentile CPU/RPS signals; KEDA's percent-based trigger and HPA percentile window sampled differently causing mismatch
2025-02-14 07:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation: increase stabilization window and enable short hysteresis to avoid immediate scale-downs
2025-02-15 12:00 UTC - Post-incident analysis started; metric collection hooks and request-level traces captured for replay
root_cause: A mismatch in aggregation semantics between KEDA trigger evaluation and HPA percentile sampling (different windows and sampling frequencies) allowed probe/request microbursts to appear as sustained signal. The autoscaler heuristics lacked sufficient debounce/hysteresis for low-sample-rate signals and did not distinguish warm-pool vs cold-start cohorts, so scale-down decisions immediately followed transient scale-ups.
mitigations_taken: Enabled 3m stabilization window on HPA to reduce sensitivity to 30s probe bursts
Added metric gating to KEDA to ignore single-sample spikes (threshold of 3 consistent samples within window)
Manual replica increase for high-impact customer namespaces during incident to reduce cold-starts
Instrumented additional tracing on probe source to verify origin of microbursts
action_items: (A1) Implement sliding-median smoothing for KEDA trigger aggregation to reduce spike sensitivity — owner: Marco Ruiz — estimate: 5 pts — status: In Progress
(A2) Add 'cohort-aware' scaling: separate warm-pool and cold-start signals so HPA honors warm-pool headroom before scaling down — owner: Priya Menon — estimate: 8 pts — status: Backlog
(A3) Align aggregation windows: standardize KEDA trigger window and HPA percentile window semantics (document and enforce) — owner: Platform infra team — estimate: 3 pts — status: Planned
(A4) Add a synthetic warmup traffic generator to CI that verifies autoscaler stability under burst patterns — owner: SRE team (Jon Chen) — estimate: 5 pts — status: Planned

(A5) Update runbook: add steps to identify fingerprint mismatches, recommended temporary knobs (stabilization window, probe gating), and customer communication templates — owner: On-call documentation owner (Aisha Patel) — estimate: 1 pt — status: In Progress

(A6) Build Grafana dashboard with 'signal overlap' visualization (KEDA trigger rate vs HPA percentile vs probe events) and alert when overlap entropy > threshold — owner: Observability (Luca Moretti) — estimate: 3 pts — status: In Progress
(A7) Post-deploy verification: run 6-hour canary in staging with synthetic probe bursts and confirm <5% increase in tail latency — owner: Testing (Ravi Gupta) — estimate: 2 pts — status: Planned
postmortem_summary: During a capacity/regression event we saw frequent oscillatory scaling driven by mismatched aggregation logic between autoscaling components. Immediate mitigations reduced impact, but systemic fixes are required: smoothing of trigger signals, cohort-aware scaling, aligned windows, and improved observability. Action items prioritize low-risk safety nets (stabilization/hysteresis) first, then algorithmic fixes and runbook/dashboards.
notes: Tradeoffs discussed: aggressive smoothing reduces false positives but increases time-to-scale for genuine sustained traffic; prioritized cohort-aware approach to avoid sacrificing responsiveness for warm traffic

Open question: whether to centralize aggregation logic in the platform controller or keep KEDA/HPA separate with strict contracts. Centralization simplifies semantics but increases coupling and blast radius.
We observed a secondary failure mode where cold-pool eviction coincided with probe jitter; follow-up investigation scheduled under ENG-948321
Customer remediation: support reached out proactively to top 5 impacted customers and offered configuration guidance for bursty workloads
